subject: Business
title: OKRs: Objectives and Key Results
description: A quick, practical guide to OKRs: Objectives and Key Results.

hook.text: Andy Grove at Intel invented OKRs. John Doerr brought them to Google. They became Silicon Valley's operating system.

buildup.text: An objective says where you want to go. Key results are the measurable milestones that prove you got there.

discovery.text: Good OKRs are ambitious but measurable. 'Improve customer satisfaction' is vague. 'Raise NPS from 30 to 50' is an OKR.

twist.text: If you hit 100% of your OKRs, they weren't ambitious enough. Google aims for 60-70% achievement.

climax.text: OKRs align entire organizations. Every team's key results connect to the company's top objectives.

punchline.text: Tell everyone where you're going. Then measure every step.

quiz.question: Why does Google aim for 60-70% OKR achievement, not 100%?
options: 100% means the goals weren't ambitious enough
They expect employees to fail regularly
OKRs are optional targets, not requirements

details.summary: OKRs are a goal-setting framework where ambitious Objectives define what you want to achieve and measurable Key Results define how you know you achieved it. Popularized by Intel and Google, OKRs align organizational efforts by making goals transparent and measurable across teams.
details.whyItMatters: OKRs provide clarity and alignment across organizations of any size. They prevent the common problem of teams working hard on activities that do not connect to strategic priorities, ensuring effort translates into meaningful business outcomes.
takeaways: Objectives are ambitious qualitative goals that inspire and direct effort
Key Results are specific measurable outcomes that prove the objective is met
Transparency across the organization aligns teams toward shared priorities

faq.question: How are OKRs different from traditional KPIs?
faq.answer: KPIs measure ongoing business health like revenue or churn rate. OKRs set ambitious forward-looking goals for specific periods, typically quarters. KPIs track what you are monitoring. OKRs define what you are trying to change. Both are useful for different purposes.

faq.question: What makes a good OKR versus a bad one?
faq.answer: Good Objectives are inspiring, qualitative, and time-bound. Good Key Results are specific, measurable, and achievable but ambitious. Bad OKRs list tasks instead of outcomes, set easy targets, or create too many objectives that dilute focus. Three to five objectives per quarter is ideal.
